component.name: PyNetboot
component.summary: Create bootable USB drives from ISO files

description.p: PyNetboot is a cross-platform tool for creating bootable USB drives from ISO files.
It allows you to create bootable Live USB drives for a variety of Linux distributions, as well as other operating systems and utilities.

ul.li: Download ISO files from various distributions automatically
Create bootable USB drives from existing ISO files
Supports Windows, macOS, and Linux
Persistent storage support for Live USB drives

description.p: PyNetboot is a Python rewrite of UNetbootin, originally created by Geza Kovacs.
Asks for your password once for the whole operation.

ul.li: Writing a drive now prompts for authentication a single time, instead of once for each privileged step
If authentication cannot be held open, each step asks separately as before, so the write still completes

description.p: Fixes copying files to the drive, and asks for your password less often.

ul.li: The drive is now mounted so that your user account can write to it. Every file previously failed to copy with a permission error, because the drive was mounted by the administrator account instead
Preparing the drive now asks for your password once rather than for each step

description.p: Records much more detail in the log, making a failed write easier to diagnose.

ul.li: The download, extraction, copy and bootloader steps each report their size, duration and outcome
The target drive's size, model and mounted partitions are recorded before anything is written to it
Copying an empty image is now reported as a failure instead of quietly producing an unbootable drive

description.p: Makes a silently empty extraction impossible.

ul.li: Unpacking an image is now confirmed to have produced files. An extraction tool that exited successfully without unpacking anything used to be taken at its word, producing a drive that could not boot but reported a completed install
If one extraction method produces nothing, the next one is tried instead of giving up

description.p: Fixes creating a bootable USB drive.

ul.li: The target drive is now given a partition table before formatting. Previously the whole disk was formatted and the boot record was then written over the filesystem's own boot sector, so the drive did not boot
The bootloader is installed to the partition and the boot record to the disk, as they require
The Flatpak now ships parted, and the disk tools are reachable at runtime

description.p: Fixes formatting a USB drive on Linux.

ul.li: Partitions on the target disk are now unmounted before formatting, which previously failed with "Device or resource busy"
Formatting errors now report the underlying cause
The software centre now shows the application name, icon and license

description.p: Renamed the project from UNetbootin to PyNetboot.

ul.li: New application ID, command name and package name
Existing settings are preserved
